method: Each field is written as a name, a width in bits and an unsigned value, and fields are laid out in the order listed from the most significant bit downward: the first field takes bits W-1 down to W-width, and the last field ends at bit 0. The widths must add up to no more than the word, and any bits left over are the low bits, which read as zero and are reported as unused. A value is accepted as decimal, 0x hex or 0b binary and is refused when it needs more bits than its field, so nothing is silently truncated; negative values are refused because the layout carries no sign convention. Words of 8, 16, 32 and 64 bits are supported, and the 64-bit case is calculated with BigInt so every bit survives. The register is shown as a fixed-width hex word, an unsigned decimal, binary grouped by byte, and as bytes in both big- and little-endian order, the latter being what a memory dump of the register usually shows on a little-endian CPU. Each field is read back out of the finished word and listed with its bit range, so the row values are a round-trip check rather than a second calculation. Fields cannot overlap because they are placed sequentially, and read-modify-write masks, reserved-bit rules, device-specific register maps and signed or fixed-point field interpretations are deliberately outside the page. Everything runs in the browser, so nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
